OffsetUnit.description: Unit of `SourceLocator.char_start/char_end`. A Unicode-scalar offset is not a byte offset.

Origin.description:
Who produced a payload. `synthetic_fixture` marks hand-made contract examples; such payloads (and
anything computed from them) can never be presented as NASA results or qualify a model.
Produced-by-the-system payloads are `system` even when their *data* is synthetic (that is
`EvidenceClass::Synthetic` / `TrainedOn::Synthetic`).

SourceLocator.description:
Where a value or passage sits inside one asset. A single locator type serves observations,
chunks, calibrations and evidence references.

Conventions fixed in C0 and checked by [`SourceLocator::validate`]:
* `asset_sha256` is the bare 64-hex digest of the asset bytes.
* `page` is the **physical** 1-based page index; the printed label goes in `page_label`.
* `char_start`/`char_end` are half-open offsets into the text of `parse_view_id`, counted in
  `offset_unit`. Offsets without a parse view and unit are legacy and not citable.
* `bbox` is `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` in fractions of the displayed page (after its /Rotate), origin
  top-left, x right, y down.
* `table_id` scopes `row`/`column` to a table inside the asset (CSV rows otherwise).

Fields added in 2.1.0 are omitted when absent, so the serialized form of older locators, and
therefore every prefix `input_hash` that embeds them, is unchanged.

description:
A citable pointer into one source version. Verifiable only against that version's asset and
parse view. Holding an `EvidenceRef` grants no access to restricted originals.

locator.description: Absent for a metadata-only citation (bytes not obtained: listing or access-gated record).

quote.description: Exact citable text from the parse view (not the normalized index text).
